beats.intro: Substitution is one way to solve a system. [[q]]Elimination is another: add the equations together so one variable cancels out.
beats.idea: Here's the idea. [[q]]x plus y equals seven, and x minus y equals one. [[stack]]Line them up, one above the other, with the x terms, y terms, and numbers in columns. [[add]]Now add the columns. x plus x is two x. [[cancel]]y plus negative y is zero: the y terms cancel. [[num]]Seven plus one is eight. [[res]]So two x equals eight, and x equals four. [[back]]Then four plus y equals seven, so y equals three. [[why]]Adding equations is allowed because both sides of each equation are equal, so the sums are equal too.
beats.mult: Often the terms don't cancel right away. [[q]]Two x plus y equals five, and three x minus two y equals negative three. [[look]]The y terms are y and negative two y. [[mul]]Multiply every term of the first equation by two: four x plus two y equals ten. [[now]]Now two y and negative two y are opposites. [[add]]Add: seven x equals seven, so x equals one. [[back]]Substitute into the first equation: two plus y equals five, so y equals three.
beats.both: Sometimes you multiply both equations. [[q]]Two x plus five y equals three, and three x plus four y equals one. [[lcm]]To eliminate x, make the x coefficients six and negative six, since six is the least common multiple of two and three. [[m1]]Multiply the first equation by three: six x plus fifteen y equals nine. [[m2]]Multiply the second by negative two: negative six x minus eight y equals negative two. [[add]]Add: seven y equals seven, so y equals one. [[back]]Then three x plus four equals one, so x equals negative one.
beats.special: Two special cases. [[inf]]If both variables cancel and you get a true statement like zero equals zero, the equations describe the same line, and there are infinitely many solutions. [[none]]If both cancel and you get something false, like zero equals negative six, there are no solutions at all.
beats.wrap: To solve by elimination, [[w1]]line up the equations with like terms in columns. [[w2]]Multiply one or both equations so a pair of coefficients are opposites. [[w3]]Add the equations to eliminate that variable, solve, and substitute back. [[end]]Now try the chapter practice.
beats.final1: Chapter practice. Solve each system by elimination.
beats.final2: Next, choose how many solutions each system has.
